static_traits.name: Zhang Hai
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, with no immediate family members
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to confide in, but often avoids talking about inadequacy out of shame; tense relationships with colleagues due to self-deprecation
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past; no psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative; tone slightly anxious; often uses absolutist and self-deprecating expressions (e.g. 'I am utterly useless' / 'I am a failure'); able to rationally identify the inconsistency between cognitions and emotions (knowing intellectually it is unreasonable, yet still believing it emotionally)

basic_info.main_problem: As long as the day's work tasks are not all completed, I keep feeling I am a useless employee. This not-good-enough feeling started months ago and keeps escalating; it has developed into fear of going to work, persistent worry about not meeting expectations, with intense anxiety appearing every shift when tasks are not yet done.
basic_info.core_demands: When these feelings began affecting my mental health and overall well-being, making it hard to enjoy daily activities like swimming and baking, I decided to seek counseling, hoping to ease anxiety and self-criticism and recover enjoyment of daily life.

core_beliefs: I am useless / a not-good-enough employee
I am not competent at work
Not completing tasks once means I am a failure

special_situations.event: Not being able to complete all the day's work tasks during a shift
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete all tasks, I am incompetent, which shows I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces herself to work harder, sets excessively high standards, pursues perfection to avoid failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am utterly useless / I am a failure

special_situations.event: The supervisor checking work or evaluating performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the supervisor thinks I am not good enough, it proves I am worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Works harder, strives for perfection in everything to avoid criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am unqualified

special_situations.event: Notices own self-deprecation in daily interactions with colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance is not perfect, colleagues will look down on me and relationships will worsen
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowers others' expectations in advance through self-deprecation to avoid harsher criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The tense relationships with colleagues are all because I am terrible

special_situations.event: Thinking of unfinished work tasks while doing leisure activities like swimming or baking
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not met work standards, I should not enjoy or relax
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stops leisure, repeatedly thinks about work, and self-blames
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not deserve enjoyment; I have not finished my tasks

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by the supervisor, seen as competent and valuable
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being criticized, negated, seen as 'not good enough'
defense_goal: Avoids criticism and failure through perfectionism and self-pressure
Preemptively deprecating oneself to lower outside expectations and reduce the risk of being negated

object_relations.self_representation: A criticized failure / an incompetent employee

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores 'not finishing a single task does not negate overall ability' and invites evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously understanding performance in black-and-white terms, believing imperfection equals failure (transference: bringing the work-setting judgment frame into counseling)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use gentle inquiry and concretizing questions, invite listing gray areas and exceptions, help distinguish single outcomes from overall ability, in a supportive, non-confrontational tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether these thoughts are reasonable, the client emphasizes 'intellectually knowing it is unreasonable', discussing the problem detached from emotions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Separates emotions from facts, tends to use rational argumentation to avoid emotional contact
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently connects emotion with bodily feeling, reduces abstract discussion, guides naming the emotions and needs, and lingers in the experience within a safe range.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about the supervisor's evaluation or others' opinions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will negate one, attributing inner self-criticism to others' thoughts (transference: projecting the inner harsh judge outward)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Do reality testing and evidence gathering, use open questions to clarify others' actual feedback, distinguish speculation from facts, in a supportive and non-evaluative tone.

manifestations: Living alone, with no immediate family members
Feeling ashamed expressing inadequacy to friends, seeking less help
Relationships with colleagues strained by self-deprecation
Past-enjoyed swimming and baking hard to enjoy
Work stress and self-blame intrude into leisure time

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeatedly using self-deprecating labels in sessions (e.g. 'I am utterly useless' / 'I am a failure')
Overly perfectionistic and cautious when setting goals
Overly concerned with the supervisor's evaluation and others' opinions

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Avoiding asking friends for help out of shame, internalizing stress as self-blame
By 'pushing myself harder', turns the need for external support into pressure on oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Assuming the supervisor will see one as 'not good enough', attributing inner self-criticism to others' views
Worrying about being looked down on when interacting with colleagues

positive_force: Willing to seek professional help, positive attitude
Strong sense of responsibility and dedication to work (a positive motivation brought by high standards)
Has a few friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Perfectionism and black-and-white thinking; often defines overall ability by a single result
Seeks external validation and is overly concerned with supervisor evaluations, prone to mind reading and personalization
Self-deprecation and labeling, frequently calling oneself 'useless' / 'a failure'
Work-related anxiety intruding into leisure, causing reduced enjoyment of life and social withdrawal

target_behavior.behavior: Engaging in self-deprecation (e.g. 'I am utterly useless' / 'I am a failure') and intense anxiety when not all tasks are completed
antecedent: Not being able to complete all the day's work tasks during a shift
When the supervisor checks or evaluates work
target_behavior.core_reason: Perfectionism and high sensitivity to external evaluation, catastrophizing a single unfinished task and defining self-worth by it
target_behavior.function: Evades the risk of being criticized, uses self-criticism to push myself to pressurize myself in pursuit of perfection
target_behavior.consequence: Fear of work and increased stress, declining confidence and productivity, tense relationships with colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids or finds it hard to enjoy leisure activities (swimming, baking), occupied by work-related rumination
antecedent: Thinking of unfinished tasks or upcoming shifts during non-work hours
target_behavior.core_reason: Constraining the self with 'should' rules: not meeting standards means not deserving rest, worrying that resting will be seen as not working hard enough
target_behavior.function: Avoids imagined guilt and criticism, maintaining a sense of control over myself through self-limitation
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased enjoyment of life, weakened resilience, impaired overall well-being
